New
Green Finance Senior Associate
Indonesia
INTRODUCTION TO GGGI

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page.
Application Deadline: Shown in the bottom of the page. All applications must be submitted by 10:00 PM (KST) on the closing date.
Position Grade: G7
Position Scale: Country Scale
End date of appointment: 31 December 2028
Salary Grade: National
Position Summary

GGGI has been assigned by the Ministry of Finance, Directorate General of Financial Sector Stability and Development, which serves as the National Designated Authority (NDA) Secretariat to implement the core functions of the NDA GCF in Indonesia, as the Delivery Partner for the Green Climate Fund (GCF) – for the implementation of “Accelerating Climate Finance Access and Delivery through Institutional Reforms in Indonesia (CLAP)” (the “Project”), funded by the GCF Readiness and Preparatory Support Program. This project will build on and complement the results obtain from the previous three GCF Readiness grants implemented in 2019-2020 (Readiness I), 2020-2022 (Readiness II), and 2023-2026 (Readiness III) with GGGI’s support.

The Green Finance Senior Associate will work under the supervision of the Project Manager of CLAP to help deliver the project. S/he will support specific project outcome results with a focus on developing a platform for enhanced climate finance access to develop and implement NDCs and another climate related target. The Senior Associate will work together with the main project counterparts and partners, including the NDA-GCF Secretariat, Ministry of Finance, technical ministries, private sectors, NGOs/CSOs, and key GCF Stakeholders.

This Senior Associate will report directly to GGGI Indonesia’s Senior Officer, Climate Finance as the Project Manager and will work three days per week at the Ministry of Finance office (project office). On other days, s/he will be working from the GGGI Jakarta office. S/he should be willing to travel.
Purpose
Support the CLAP Project Manager in the development and implementation of the CLAP project.

Adopt and apply technical knowledge to deliver a portfolio of analytical services focused on a coherent evidence-based policy and regulatory reform process to accelerate investments in climate change-related projects.

Support in delivering Project Outcome 1 focusing on the development of Climate Finance Tracking system, by providing technical inputs to overall system design and support in facilitating the consultation with the relevant stakeholders.
Provide hands-on support and technical inputs on accreditation process and technical recommendation for nominated/candidate National Direct Accredited Entities (DAEs).
Provide technical advice on green and sustainable finance issues, particularly in developing sustainable finance frameworks and guidelines for financial institutions.

Initiate and conduct relevant workshops, dialogues, focus group discussions, and consultations with key national and subnational stakeholders from both public and private sector/financial institutions.

Provide technical support in facilitating regular coordination meetings with the Climate Finance Focal Points (CFFP) including preparation of materials, meeting reports, and facilitate a series of discussions with relevant stakeholders in harmonizing the climate finance data, as well as identify new potential key focal points to be included in the CFFP.
Support the Project Manager to carry out administrative and operational tasks of the CLAP project.
Prepare internal and external project reports.
Engagement
Support the Project Manager in implementing project activities in close cooperation with the NDA Secretariat’s Technical Team.

Led by the Project Manager, work closely with key partners, including the Ministry of Finance as the NDA-GCF Secretariat, technical ministries, local governments, private sector/financial institutions, and other relevant stakeholders.
Independently manage the technical team’s outputs (consisting of consultants from various fields) to meet challenging timelines and ensure successful quality delivery in line with the agreed outputs.
Led by the Project Manager, support the engagement with financial regulators and provide technical inputs for finance policy development and decision-making.
Support in building a coordination and communication with the nominated/candidate DAEs to provide technical assistance on GCF accreditation process.
Support in maintaining regular coordination meetings with the Climate Finance Focal Points, particularly in harmonizing the climate finance data.
Delivery
Provide analysis and technical inputs into the review, development, and assessment of the Climate Finance Tracking system and support consultations with relevant Climate Finance Focal Points.

Facilitate and aligning the result of existing climate finance governance study and initiative with the CFFP targets and workplan, as a feedback and input for the design of climate finance tracking system.

Support the Project Manager in providing technical inputs in developing of sustainable finance frameworks and guidelines for financial institutions, including coordinating with key stakeholders such as OJK, Bank of Indonesia, and financial institutions. Identify the needs and gaps in the existing framework and develop concepts to strengthen Indonesia's sustainable finance framework.
Provide technical advice on sustainable finance and GCF accreditation process to the Ministry of Finance, as the NDA GCF, and DAE(s);
Support the Project Manager to prepare monthly and annual reports in accordance with the monitoring mechanism set by GGGI and the GCF.
Prepare briefing notes and analytical reports to support GGGI’s green and climate finance work in Indonesia.
Ensure the principles of gender equality and social inclusion are effectively reflected in all relevant activities including in programme reports, workplans, and technical advice provided to NDA.
Uphold GGGI’s values.
REQUIREMENTS
QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree relevant to environmental, economics, climate finance, sustainable finance, or related fields.
At least 3 (three) years of experience in country-level work experience with climate and green finance/investment is highly desirable.
A good track record of working on project development, green investment processes, banking and non-banking sector, and public sector finance is desirable.
Proven track record in planning, reporting, and financial management.
Experience and knowledge of green finance in Indonesia, climate related projects, green growth, and sustainable development.
In-depth familiarity with GCF accreditation processes is highly desirable.
Experience in stakeholder engagement and working with inter-institutional programmes.
Ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds.
Excellent English and Indonesian oral and written communication skills, including public speaking.
FUNCTIONAL
Ability to develop and maintain strong relationships with GGGI partner institutions.
Experience in policy formulation, capacity building and multi-stakeholder engagement.
Ability to understand Government policy and strategy formulation and implementation mechanisms at national and sub-national levels within a multi-sectoral and cross-sectoral context in Indonesia.
Excellent organizational and management skills and demonstrated experience in successfully mainstreaming of safeguards, gender, poverty reduction and social inclusion.
Demonstrated understanding of principles of green investment and climate financing.
Ability to manage projects that are supported by international and local consultants.
Ability to work in an organized, systematic manner, with degree of innovations and decision-making abilities.
Ability to write concise and clear reports and meeting minutes and to file them effectively and develop and maintain the GGGI database accordingly.
Ability to perform in demanding atmosphere and self-motivate to produce quality results in timely manner.
CORPORATE
Understand and actively support GGGI’s mission, vision and values.
Promote an organizational culture of trust, transparency, respect and partnership.
Excels at problem solving, asks questions and seeks support when needed, easily shares information and knowledge with others both internally as externally.
Manage emotions and stress positively, build rapport and resolves conflict easily.
Strong ability to work independently and/or remotely, while maintaining productivity.
Work Conditions
Senior Officer is an G7 grade level in GGGI’s National salary scale. Determination of base salary is subject to candidate's experience, academic background and internal equity.
GGGI provides 15% of base salary towards retirement plan/long-term savings, 27 days of annual leave, and private health insurance that covers dental and vision.

GGGI is committed to providing a work environment that is sufficiently flexible to accommodate diverse life-cycle challenges and assist Staff members to achieve a better balance between work and personal/family commitments, thus ensuring high performance, long-term productivity, and well-being of Staff members.
The chosen candidate is expected to be based in Jakarta, Indonesia, and will report to the Senior Climate Finance Officer of the GGGI Indonesia, serves as the Program Manager (also based in Jakarta).
This is a national position and does not include relocation benefits
PROJECT INTRODUCTION

GGGI supports the Government of Indonesia (GoI) under the joint GoI-GGGI Green Indonesia Future Initiative Program (GIFT, “the Program”). The Program aims to demonstrate that green investments can become the norm both for investors and planners, ultimately improving the quality of economic development for more environmental sustainability and social inclusion. Through the Program, GGGI collaborates with the Ministry of Development Planning (BAPPENAS) as program host, the Coordinating Ministry of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Forestry, PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur (“PT SMI”) , Indonesia Environment Fund (IEF), and others.

In October 2026, the Readiness Proposal for Indonesia, titled Accelerating Climate Finance Access and Delivery through Institutional Reforms in Indonesia has been approved by the GCF Secretariat. Funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF), this 4-years GCF Multiyear Readiness Program will help to strengthen Indonesia’s institutional capacity, governance framework, and strategic planning to mobilize and manage climate finance effectively. Building on lessons from previous Readiness Phases, current program addresses systemic gaps that hinder Indonesia’s ability to access and deploy climate finance at scale, while aligning with national climate priorities and the GCF 2024-2027 Readiness Strategy. It consists of a range of activities with the objective of achieving three main readiness outcomes which will directly contribute to the GCF Readiness Outcomes under the 2024-2027 strategy:
Outcome 1: Strengthened NDA capacity and strategic frameworks for NDC, NAP, and LTS implementation.
Outcome 2: Development of four high-quality concept notes aligned with NCFS programming targets.
Outcome 3: Enhanced knowledge-sharing and regional collaboration to scale climate finance innovation.

Child protection – GGGI is committed to child protection, irrespective of whether any specific area of work involves direct contact with children. GGGI’s Child Protection Policy is written in accordance with the Convention on the Rights of the Child.
